title: Day 4 — Navigate a Codebase & Ship a Feature
prompt: You're dropped into a small library-catalog package. The repository layer is done; three service methods (checkout, return_book, most_borrowed) are stubbed. Implement them to pass the integration tests. How do you get oriented?

clarifications.answer: Read repository.py first — it already gives you active_loans_for, has_active_loan, add_loan, remove_loan, and borrow_count. Use them; don't reinvent storage.
checkout: reject if no copies available or the member already holds this book; otherwise record the loan.
return_book: if the member has no active loan for that book, raise ValueError; otherwise remove the loan.
most_borrowed(n): top n books by cumulative times ever borrowed, ties broken by title; exclude books never borrowed.
available_copies is total minus ACTIVE loans; borrow_count is CUMULATIVE (it doesn't drop on return) — two different counters.

hints: Map the repository API first — one line per method — before writing any service code.
checkout uses available_copies + has_active_loan; return_book uses remove_loan's bool result.
most_borrowed: filter books with borrow_count > 0, then sort by (-borrow_count, title)[:n].
